newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, tone cautious.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, tone cautious.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices held their ground in late trading on Wednesday but an upturn in Malaysian prices made some sellers hold back, traders said.
They said olein was around 1,440 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but some quotes were heard at 1,445 rupiah.
"I'm glad I did not sell very much before (Malaysian) prices starting rising," one trader said. "The local market was rather quiet after the rise as everyone wanted to wait and see."
Malaysian prices soared following news that Indonesia's joint marketing agency (KPB) was suspending crude palm oil exports in October to meet a backlog of previous commitments.

A KPB official told Reuters the agency would not be signing any new export contract this month, but would meet all existing contracts. State plantations channell all their output through the KPB, which exports 30 percent and sells the rest locally.
Traders said the move was not expected to have any direct impact on the local market, which could, however, be lifted by rising overseas' prices due to a supply squeeze.
"Overseas' markets could see a disappearance of more than 100,000 tonnes because of the move," one trader said. "But I am not sure how much will be from the spot or forward markets."
